title: Diagnose an incident from logs
summary: Đọc log tiếng Anh, tách signal khỏi noise và viết chẩn đoán có bằng chứng.
learningObjectives: Xác định symptom và tín hiệu quan sát được
Đề xuất kiểm tra có thể bác bỏ hypothesis

sections.title: Checkout logs
sections.content:
Synthetic training artifact — non-production. 10:02 INFO request started id=91
10:02 WARN retry payment-provider attempt=2
10:03 ERROR connection pool exhausted active=50 max=50
10:03 ERROR checkout failed id=91 status=503

expressions.meaning: Nêu observation có thể truy ngược trực tiếp về log.
expressions.example: The log shows request 91 returning HTTP 503 at 10:03.

expressions.phrase: This may indicate ___, but it does not prove ___.
expressions.meaning: Nối evidence với hypothesis mà không khẳng định root cause.
expressions.example: This may indicate that pool exhaustion contributed to the failure, but it does not prove the pool type or root cause.
alternatives: One possible explanation is ___; the evidence does not yet confirm it.

expressions.phrase: To test this, compare ___ with ___; if ___, reject the hypothesis.
expressions.meaning: Đề xuất một kiểm tra có kết quả đủ để làm yếu hoặc bác bỏ hypothesis.
expressions.example: To test this, compare wait and release metrics with a healthy window; if they remain normal, reject the pool hypothesis.
alternatives: Check ___ next; normal results would point away from ___.

exercises.question: Dòng nào là tín hiệu trực tiếp mạnh nhất cần điều tra?
exercises.explanation: Dòng này cho thấy một pool chưa xác định đã chạm giới hạn ngay trước lỗi 503; nó hỗ trợ hypothesis về pool exhaustion nhưng chưa xác định pool type hoặc root cause.

exercises.question: Câu nào chỉ nêu fact có trong log, không thêm root cause?
options: The payment provider caused the checkout failure.
A database leak exhausted the connection pool.
exercises.explanation: Request id, status và timestamp xuất hiện trực tiếp; payment-provider cause, database pool type và leak đều chưa được xác nhận.

exercises.question: Bước nào có thể làm yếu pool-exhaustion hypothesis nếu kết quả bình thường?
options: Compare pool wait and release metrics with a healthy window.
Repeat that the pool was exhausted in the incident channel.
Assume the unnamed pool is the database pool and restart it.
correctAnswer: Compare pool wait and release metrics with a healthy window.
exercises.explanation: Normal wait and release metrics would point away from pool exhaustion; repeating or assuming the cause cannot test the hypothesis.

performanceTask.title: Write an evidence-based diagnosis
performanceTask.scenario: Checkout trả 503 và bạn cần gửi chẩn đoán ban đầu cho on-call engineer.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: Read the log once, hide it, then write the initial diagnosis in English from memory.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: Viết bằng tiếng Anh symptom, probable cause, evidence và next verification step. Phân biệt fact với hypothesis.
performanceTask.modelResponse: Checkout request 91 returned HTTP 503 at 10:03. Immediately beforehand, an unnamed pool reported active=50 and max=50. My hypothesis is that pool exhaustion contributed to the failure, but the excerpt does not identify the pool type or explain why capacity was exhausted. Next, inspect wait time and connection-release metrics for the same request window, then compare them with a healthy window. If those signals stay normal, reject the pool-exhaustion hypothesis and investigate the payment-provider retries instead.
performanceTask.retryPrompt: Sửa chẩn đoán để mỗi hypothesis có evidence và một bước kiểm chứng.
performanceTask.transferPrompt: Đọc unseen worker log được hiển thị rồi viết bằng tiếng Anh fact, một cautious hypothesis và verification step. Không suy ra một memory trend từ chỉ một sample.
performanceTask.reviewPrompt: Từ một unseen log mới, tóm tắt fact, hypothesis và verification step sau khi source đã ẩn.

trainingSource.title: Queue latency logs
trainingSource.content:
Synthetic training artifact — non-production. 11:00 INFO queue_depth=120 baseline=90
11:05 WARN queue_depth=2400 oldest_age=14m
11:05 INFO consumers=2 baseline=12
11:06 ERROR sla_breached threshold=5m

extractionItems.question: What is the observed symptom?
options: The oldest message is 14 minutes old, above the five-minute SLA
The queue currently has twelve consumers
extractionItems.correctAnswer: The oldest message is 14 minutes old, above the five-minute SLA
extractionItems.feedback: The oldest age and SLA threshold are observed; twelve consumers is the baseline, not the current count.

extractionItems.question: Which signal supports the nearest hypothesis?
options: Consumers dropped from twelve to two
extractionItems.correctAnswer: Consumers dropped from twelve to two
extractionItems.feedback: Reduced consumer capacity can explain the growing queue.

extractionItems.question: What observation would best test whether reduced consumer capacity caused the backlog?
options: Restore consumer capacity and check whether processing throughput rises while backlog and oldest age fall
Ask only why ten consumers stopped
extractionItems.correctAnswer: Restore consumer capacity and check whether processing throughput rises while backlog and oldest age fall
extractionItems.feedback: A throughput increase together with a falling backlog tests the proposed cause; asking why consumers stopped investigates a different question.

readingLadder.applicationPrompt: Apply fact → cautious hypothesis → falsifiable check to the displayed queue latency logs. Compare processing throughput with message arrivals, then check whether the backlog and oldest age fall after consumer capacity is restored.
applicationChecklist: I kept facts separate from hypotheses.
I proposed a check that could disprove the hypothesis.

rubric.label: Observed symptom
rubric.description: Names the failure and relevant context accurately.

rubric.label: Evidence-backed hypothesis
rubric.description: Connects a log signal to a cautious probable cause.

rubric.label: Verification step
rubric.description: Proposes a concrete next check that could confirm or reject the hypothesis.
